title: Mario & Luigi: Partners in Time
subtitle: The brothers meet themselves
summary: Mario & Luigi: Partners in Time is AlphaDream's Nintendo DS role-playing adventure about a rescue across the Mushroom Kingdom's past and present. Mario and Luigi meet their infant selves while following Princess Peach into a conflict with the invading Shroobs. body: Mario & Luigi: Partners in Time is AlphaDream's Nintendo DS role-playing adventure about a rescue across the Mushroom Kingdom's past and present. Mario and Luigi meet their infant selves while following Princess Peach into a conflict with the invading Shroobs. The four heroes travel together, but their different sizes and abilities allow them to separate when a route requires it. The comedy comes from seeing the brothers confront another version of themselves; the game turns that same idea into a practical arrangement for exploration and combat.

Each hero is associated with a face button, extending the series' timed actions from a pair of brothers to a group of four. Battles remain turn-based, but well-timed inputs strengthen attacks and help the characters respond to incoming blows. The player must recognise which member of the party needs to act. That relationship makes the team tangible through the controls: the babies are not simply additional portraits in a menu. Their presence asks for another layer of coordination during otherwise familiar jumps, hammers and defensive actions.

Adults and babies can split up, letting the younger pair reach places the older brothers cannot. The DS screens help keep the separated groups visible, while the ordinary travelling view uses the upper screen for a map. Progress depends on bringing these different routes back into the same objective. AlphaDream builds its time-travel premise into the player's handling of space: the same character can be large or small, and a barrier for one version becomes an invitation to hand the next action to the other.
story_headings: A smaller route through the world
